title: When Shipwrecks Become Reefs
subtitle: 雅思風格 Part 4 講課：沉船如何成為人工魚礁，以及學界的不同看法

sentences.en: Good afternoon. In today's lecture I'll be looking at what happens to a ship once it sinks, and in particular how wrecks can turn into artificial reefs.
sentences.zh: 午安。今天的講課我要探討船沉沒之後會發生什麼事，特別是沉船如何變成人工魚礁。

highlights.text: in particular how wrecks can turn into artificial reefs
highlights.note: 講課主題句：Part 4 第一題常問講者要談什麼。

examples.en: Divers explored the wreck.
examples.zh: 潛水員探索了那艘沉船。

examples.en: Old trains were sunk to make an artificial reef.
examples.zh: 舊火車被沉入海中做成人工魚礁。

chunks.text: Good afternoon.
In today's lecture I'll be looking at what happens to a ship
chunks.zh: 今天的講課我要探討船會發生什麼事

chunks.text: once it sinks,
and in particular how wrecks can turn into artificial reefs.
chunks.zh: 特別是沉船如何變成人工魚礁。

sentences.en: You might assume that a sunken vessel is simply a form of pollution, and in some cases, that's exactly what it is.
sentences.zh: 你可能會以為沉船只是一種污染，而在某些情況下，它確實就是。

examples.en: Don't assume everyone knows the rules.
examples.zh: 別以為每個人都知道規則。

examples.en: The vessel left port at dawn.
examples.zh: 那艘船在黎明時離港。

grammar.explanation: sunken 是 sink 的過去分詞形容詞用法，放在名詞前表示「沉沒的」。動詞過去分詞一般用 sunk。

examples.en: They found sunken treasure.
examples.zh: 他們找到了沉沒的寶藏。

grammar.pitfall: 名詞前用 sunken，被動句用 sunk：The ship was sunk.

sentences.en: However, if a ship has been properly cleaned of fuel and other hazardous materials beforehand, it can become remarkably productive habitat.
sentences.zh: 然而，如果船事先徹底清除了燃料和其他有害物質，它就能成為生產力驚人的棲地。

highlights.text: properly cleaned of fuel and other hazardous materials beforehand
highlights.note: 關鍵條件：要先清除燃料與有害物質，才能成為好的棲地。

examples.en: Hazardous waste must be handled carefully.
examples.zh: 有害廢棄物必須小心處理。

examples.en: Wetlands are an important habitat for birds.
examples.zh: 濕地是鳥類的重要棲地。

examples.en: The old car runs remarkably well.
examples.zh: 這輛舊車跑得出奇地好。

chunks.text: However,
if a ship has been properly cleaned of fuel and other hazardous materials beforehand,
chunks.zh: 如果船事先徹底清除了燃料和其他有害物質，

chunks.text: it can become remarkably productive habitat.
chunks.zh: 它就能成為生產力驚人的棲地。

sentences.en: The process begins within days, as bacteria and algae form a thin film over the hull.
sentences.zh: 這個過程在幾天內就開始了，細菌和藻類會在船身上形成一層薄膜。

examples.en: Algae turned the pond green.
examples.zh: 藻類讓池塘變成綠色。

examples.en: The hull was painted white.
examples.zh: 船身被漆成白色。

grammar.explanation: as 在這裡表示「隨著…；在…的同時」，帶出和主要子句同時發生的過程。

examples.en: As the sun rose, the birds began to sing.
examples.zh: 太陽升起時，鳥兒開始歌唱。

grammar.pitfall: as 有多種意思（因為、當、如同），要從上下文判斷。

sentences.en: This film, in turn, attracts small grazing animals, which then draw in the fish that feed on them.
sentences.zh: 這層膜接著會吸引以啃食為生的小動物，而這些小動物又會引來以牠們為食的魚。

highlights.note: 表示連鎖反應：A 引起 B，B 再引起 C。講課中描述過程時很常見。

examples.en: Rain feeds the grass, which in turn feeds the cows.
examples.zh: 雨水滋養青草，青草再餵養牛群。

examples.en: Owls feed on mice.
examples.zh: 貓頭鷹以老鼠為食。

chunks.text: This film, in turn,
attracts small grazing animals,
which then draw in the fish
that feed on them.

sentences.en: Within a few years, corals and sponges may have colonised the steel, and the wreck starts to function much like a natural reef.
sentences.zh: 幾年之內，珊瑚和海綿可能已經佈滿鋼板，沉船就開始發揮和天然礁石非常相似的功能。

vocab.zh: （生物）移居、佔據（英式拼法，美式為 colonize）

examples.en: Plants quickly colonised the empty land.
examples.zh: 植物很快就佔據了那塊空地。

examples.en: The room functions as an office.
examples.zh: 這個房間當作辦公室使用。

grammar.explanation: may have + 過去分詞在這裡表示「到那時可能已經…」，推測某時間點前完成的事。

examples.en: By then, they may have left.
examples.zh: 到那時他們可能已經走了。

grammar.pitfall: 不要寫成 may have colonise，have 後面要接過去分詞。

sentences.en: Researchers have found that the shape of the structure matters a great deal.
sentences.zh: 研究人員發現，結構的形狀非常重要。

examples.en: What you eat really matters.
examples.zh: 你吃什麼真的很重要。

examples.en: Her advice helped me a great deal.
examples.zh: 她的建議幫了我很大的忙。

sentences.en: Wrecks with plenty of openings and sheltered spaces tend to support a wider variety of species than flat, exposed surfaces do.
sentences.zh: 有許多開口和遮蔽空間的沉船，往往比平坦、暴露的表面能養活更多樣的物種。

highlights.note: 比較的結論：結構複雜的沉船物種較多。

examples.en: We ate lunch in a sheltered spot.
examples.zh: 我們在一個避風的地方吃午餐。

examples.en: The hill is exposed to strong winds.
examples.zh: 這座山丘直接受強風吹襲。

grammar.explanation: 比較句中用 do 代替前面的動詞 support，避免重複。

examples.en: She runs faster than I do.
examples.zh: 她跑得比我快。

grammar.pitfall: do 要配合主詞：複數主詞用 do，單數用 does。

chunks.text: Wrecks with plenty of openings and sheltered spaces
chunks.zh: 有很多開口和遮蔽空間的沉船

chunks.text: tend to support a wider variety of species
chunks.zh: 往往養活更多樣的物種

chunks.text: than flat, exposed surfaces do.

sentences.en: That said, artificial reefs are not without their critics.
sentences.zh: 話雖如此，人工魚礁也有批評者。

highlights.note: 轉折訊號：接下來要講反面意見。

examples.en: It's expensive. That said, it's worth it.
examples.zh: 它很貴。話雖如此，還是值得。

examples.en: The plan has many critics.
examples.zh: 這個計畫有很多人批評。

grammar.explanation: not without 是雙重否定，意思是「並非沒有」，也就是「確實有」。

examples.en: The trip was not without problems.
examples.zh: 這趟旅行也不是沒出問題。

grammar.pitfall: 不要理解成「沒有批評者」，雙重否定等於肯定。

sentences.en: Some ecologists argue that they don't actually increase the number of fish, but merely gather existing populations into one spot, where they're easier to catch.
sentences.zh: 有些生態學家認為，人工魚礁其實沒有增加魚的數量，只是把原有的族群集中到一個地方，讓牠們更容易被捕撈。

highlights.text: merely gather existing populations into one spot
highlights.note: 批評的核心論點：只是聚集，不是增加。

examples.en: The ecologist studied the river.
examples.zh: 那位生態學家研究這條河。

examples.en: It was merely a joke.
examples.zh: 那只不過是個玩笑。

grammar.quote: don't actually increase the number of fish, but merely gather
grammar.explanation: not A but B 表示「不是 A 而是 B」，merely 加強「只是」的語氣。

examples.en: He didn't win, but merely finished.
examples.zh: 他沒有贏，只是跑完了。

grammar.pitfall: but 後面的動詞要和前面的動詞形式一致。

chunks.text: Some ecologists argue
that they don't actually increase the number of fish,
chunks.zh: 它們其實沒有增加魚的數量，

chunks.text: but merely gather existing populations into one spot,
chunks.zh: 只是把原有族群集中到一處，

chunks.text: where they're easier to catch.

sentences.en: This is a genuine concern, and it's one reason why fishing is often restricted around newly sunk wrecks.
sentences.zh: 這是一個確實存在的疑慮，也是新沉放的船骸周圍常常限制捕魚的原因之一。

examples.en: She showed genuine interest in the project.
examples.zh: 她對這個計畫展現真誠的興趣。

examples.en: Parking is restricted on this street.
examples.zh: 這條街限制停車。

grammar.quote: one reason why fishing is often restricted
grammar.explanation: reason why + 子句，說明某事的原因；why 也可以省略。

examples.en: That's the reason why I left.
examples.zh: 這就是我離開的原因。

grammar.pitfall: 不要寫成 the reason because。

sentences.en: So, for your assignment, I'd like you to weigh up both positions, drawing on at least two case studies from the reading list.
sentences.zh: 所以，你們的作業是要權衡這兩種立場，並至少引用閱讀清單上的兩個案例研究。

highlights.note: 作業要求：比較兩方觀點，是 Part 4 結尾常考的細節。

examples.en: We need to weigh up the costs.
examples.zh: 我們需要權衡成本。

examples.en: She drew on her own life for the novel.
examples.zh: 她以自己的人生為小說取材。

examples.en: The book includes three case studies.
examples.zh: 這本書收錄了三個案例研究。

chunks.text: So, for your assignment,
I'd like you to weigh up both positions,
chunks.zh: 我希望你們權衡兩種立場，

chunks.text: drawing on at least two case studies
chunks.zh: 引用至少兩個案例研究

chunks.text: from the reading list.
